prompt: Implement Quantum Phase Estimation with a 3-qubit counting register (qubits 0, 1, 2; qubit 0 is least significant) and a 1-qubit eigenstate register (qubit 3). The eigenstate is |1> of the phase gate P(3*pi/4) (i.e. P(theta)|1> = e^{i*theta}|1>, theta = 3*pi/4) — initialize qubit 3 to |1> with an X gate. Steps: Hadamard on qubits 0-2; apply controlled-P(theta * 2^j) from counting qubit j onto qubit 3, for j = 0, 1, 2 (so angles 3*pi/4, 3*pi/2, 3*pi respectively); apply the standard inverse Quantum Fourier Transform (Qiskit's conventional ordering, i.e. the exact inverse of the QFT convention used in the qft_Nq tasks) to the counting register (qubits 0-2) only. The phase 3/8 is exactly representable in 3 bits, so the counting register lands EXACTLY on qubit 0 = |1>, qubit 1 = |1>, qubit 2 = |0> (binary for 3, qubit 0 least significant) with certainty — this is a deterministic target, not an approximation. Return the resulting 4-qubit state; no measurement.
